spi: logos-contract checker v1 - ADR 0031 D5: an annotated closed-model certificate, checked relative to its semiring's identity (#1821 P9 I5a)
note: HAND-AUTHORED from ADR 0031 D5 and rulings Q14/Q15 on #1821 (2026-11-12): every expected element is worked out by hand from the algebra; no core produced any of it. NOTATION: `profile`, `extensional`, `edb`, `program` and each case's `cert` follow vectors/negation.json (the negation_v1 profile: the lt theory; EDB leaves = `extensional`; the cert bound to the context derived from the live program). Elements follow vectors/semiring.json's value grammar. `semiring` names the semiring the checker is given and `cert_semiring` the one whose identity the annotated cert names: counting, tropical and stopping are vectors/semiring.json's (stopping is its fixture: every operation on elements stops at the capacity bound); fold_order is this file's TEST semiring, defined by each core's replay and never registered: declared identity (fixture/fold-order, 1, 32 zero bytes), no law declared, carrier every Atom, zero and one the empty atom, add(x, y) and mul(x, y) both the atom of x's bytes then y's bytes. Its add is order-sensitive on purpose (Q15 condition 3). `annotations` lists one {pred, elements} per sealed table, in the cert's table order, one element per row in row order. THE CHECK, in order: (1) the checker's semiring identity must equal the cert's (annotation_identity_mismatch); (2) the cert passes the boolean check as a one-cert world (reject_cert, its code unchanged); (3) a partial scope, a negated or count literal in a scope clause, or a grounding whose body is not decided is annotation_unsupported; (4) every sealed table is annotated in order with one element per row, each an element of the semiring (annotation_shape, naming the row for a non-element); (5) the IDB rows (every row of a table whose predicate is not extensional) are recomputed as the least solution of a(t) = the left fold, from zero, with add over t's groundings in canonical order, of the left fold, from one, with mul over the grounding's positive non-theory body literals in body order, of each literal's element (an extensional row's claimed element, which is a premise; an IDB row's previous-round value). The groundings are the closure join's body-true groundings of every scope clause with an IDB head; canonical order is ascending codec bytes of Tuple[Atom(clause id), Tuple[Tuple[Atom(var), value of its image]...]] with the variables in ascending byte order. Rounds are Jacobi from zero, bounded at (IDB rows + 1); no fixed point within the bound is annotation_not_converged; an add or mul that answers not-an-element or stopped is semiring_not_an_element or semiring_stopped, naming the IDB row being computed; then the first IDB row whose claim differs is annotation_mismatch. `outcome` is accept, reject (an annotation code) or reject_cert (the boolean check's code); `expected` carries the code, the `row` (pred, index) where one is named, and for accept the law relied on (kleene_least_fixpoint when the ground dependency graph over IDB rows has a cycle, else null), and `unattested`, the extensional tables whose elements were premises bound by the digest, never attested (Q15 condition 1), in the cert's table order.
